thread:
Elaine Morris: Hey team, customer app (Acme) started failing JSON parsing after today's deploy. In their logs the Redwood response shows two top-level JSON objects back-to-back.
Maya Patel: Thanks Elaine — can you paste the exact response snippet and the request_id? Also, did they use streaming=true or standard sync calls?
Elaine Morris: request_id=req-8f3c4b, model=redwood-2. Sample response attached (trimmed):
```json
{"order": {"id": 123, "status": "shipped"}}
{"order": {"id": 124, "status": "pending"}}
```
Elaine Morris: The client expects a single JSON object (json_mode=structured) and our parser errors on the second object.
Maya Patel: Got it. That looks like newline-delimited JSON (NDJSON) but sent without explicit ndjson mode. Were they using streaming? If streaming=true the client needs to handle multiple chunks.
Elaine Morris: They said streaming=false. It came back in one HTTP response body exactly like that.
Raj Singh: Hmm. Two plausible causes: model produced extra JSON after a fallback, or our response-assembler merged two separate messages into one body without adding a separator header. Repro steps requested.
Raj Singh: Can you share the full request payload (no PII) — particularly any json_schema / structured_output flags? Also the response headers (Content-Type).
Elaine Morris: Payload has: "structured_output": {"mode": "json", "schema": "order_schema_v2"}. Content-Type: application/json; charset=utf-8. No chunked transfer indicated.
Raj Singh: Thanks. Short-term workaround: update client parser to be tolerant — split on newline and parse each top-level JSON object separately (most robust for NDJSON-like responses). Also, if the app expects a single object, set the model call to include a wrapper schema (e.g., {"orders": [<items>]} ) or request explicitly "json_mode":"single_object" if possible.
Maya Patel: I'll escalate to infra to check response assembly. @infra-bot can you pull request logs for req-8f3c4b and any streaming flag mismatches around 2025-06-03T14:45Z?
infra-bot: fetched logs for req-8f3c4b. Attached event sequence: model-response(partial)->fallback-variant(overlap)->response-flush. Suggests two terminal chunks were flushed without a joiner.
Raj Singh: That aligns. We'll open an internal bug: server may be concatenating two JSON fragments when a fallback occurs. Priority P1 for correctness (customers parsing structured output). Target: hotfix in next release cycle and a rollback if high hit rate.
Maya Patel: SLA/customer comms — we'll reply to Acme within 2 business hours acknowledging impact and provide the parsing workaround. ETA for root-cause and patch: 48 hours. Any objections?
Raj Singh: fine by me.
Elaine Morris: I'll send the workaround + temporary parser snippet to the customer now and let them know we're investigating. They'll handle client-side split for the moment.
Maya Patel: Thanks. Please attach the snippet I drafted:
```js
// tolerant NDJSON split workaround
const text = await res.text();
const objs = text.trim().split(/\n+/).map(s => JSON.parse(s));
// merge or take first depending on your contract
```
Elaine Morris: Sent to Acme. Customer acknowledged :thumbsup: and asked for a formal incident update when available.
Raj Singh: I'll start the bug and link the test that reproduces multi-object outputs. Adding unit test to ensure we never emit multiple top-level objects in single-response mode.
Maya Patel: Closing loop: created bug INF-4821, assigned to runtime team. Will post updates in this thread.
infra-bot: INF-4821 created by Raj Singh. Priority: P1. ETA patch window: 2025-06-05.
Maya Patel: Thanks everyone, marking this as active until patch verified. :white_check_mark:
